cards.explanation: The city will be captured. The text says, "For I will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem, and the city will be captured…" (Zechariah 14:2). It's a hard line, friends, and I won't dress it up. But keep listening, because this prophecy has a whole lot more to say.

The answer is True. The text says, "Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be removed from the city." (Zechariah 14:2). So even in the middle of the capture, some people stay put. Half leave, half remain.

The LORD is the One who goes out. "Then the LORD will go out to fight against those nations, as He fights in the day of battle." (Zechariah 14:3). No army gets named as the one who steps in. After a verse about a captured city, that's a turn worth noticing, friends.

The people will flee through the valley. "You will flee by My mountain valley, for it will extend to Azal." (Zechariah 14:5). The Mount of Olives is split in two, forming a great valley (Zechariah 14:4). The mountain splits and the valley becomes the way out. That's quite a hallway to have appear out of nowhere.

All the holy ones come with Him. "Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him." (Zechariah 14:5). He arrives with company. The text doesn't tell us more than that, so I won't either. It comes right after the verse about fleeing through the valley.

The answer is False. The text says, "but when evening comes, there will be light." (Zechariah 14:7). It's a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night. Evening shows up and the light shows up with it. That's not the usual order at all.

The answer is True. "…living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it toward the Eastern Sea and the other half toward the Western Sea, in summer and winter alike." (Zechariah 14:8). Half of it heads toward each sea. Any season, it keeps flowing. I've never had an oven that steady.

The word is King. "On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth…" (Zechariah 14:9). Not over one city or one land, but all the earth. The verse goes on, "…the LORD alone, and His name alone." (Zechariah 14:9).

The answer is False. The verse says, "…the LORD alone, and His name alone." (Zechariah 14:9). He becomes King over all the earth, and the nations' gods are not mentioned as sharing it. The word is alone.

The answer is False. The text says, "People will live there, and never again will there be an utter destruction. So Jerusalem will dwell securely." (Zechariah 14:11). Just before that, the city "…will be raised up and will remain in her place…" (Zechariah 14:10). Never again is a big promise, friends, and the city dwells securely. So no second round of utter destruction is coming.

They will turn on each other. The text says, "…each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will rise against the other." (Zechariah 14:13). The panic comes from the LORD. This is another heavy part, and it's okay to let it sit.

The wealth will be collected in great abundance. "…the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be collected…" (Zechariah 14:14). The verse says that wealth is gold, silver and clothing, piled up. It's in the same verse that says Judah will also fight at Jerusalem. I've never seen a cookie box that full.

They go up to worship the King. "Then all the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts…" (Zechariah 14:16). Survivors from the very nations that came against Jerusalem are the ones going up to worship. And they go year after year, friends.

The feast is the Feast of Tabernacles. They go up "…to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles." (Zechariah 14:16). The prophecy names it again in verses 18 and 19. So this feast is no side note here.

The word is rain. The text says, "And should any of the families of the earth not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, then the rain will not fall on them." (Zechariah 14:17). The rain is what's held back. It's about families of the earth, not just one nation.

The cooking pots will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar. "…the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar." (Zechariah 14:20). The everyday pots are put right alongside those bowls, and that's a big step up for a cooking pot. Then verse 21 says every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts.

The answer is True. The last line of the passage says, "And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 14:21). That's how the passage ends, friends. The text doesn't say more than that.
